result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.domirank_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get DomiRank centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16377-L16579){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.domirank_centrality( sigma=None, alpha=0.95, method="iterative", tolerance=1e-05, max_iter=1000, patience=10, max_depth=50, return_sigma=False, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} DomiRank centrality quantifies node dominance in their neighborhoods. The competition parameter sigma (or alpha) provides a tunable trade-off between local and global topological information: `d𝚪ᵢ(t)/dt = σ(dᵢ - Σⱼ Aᵢⱼ 𝚪ⱼ(t)) - 𝚪ᵢ(t)` Where: - `𝚪ᵢ` is the dominance score for node `i` - `σ` is the competition parameter - `dᵢ` is the degree of node `i` - `A` is the adjacency matrix Unlike eigenvector-type centralities (where being connected to important nodes makes you important), DomiRank identifies nodes that dominate their local structure. Being close to a dominant node can suppress your own dominance in high-competition contexts. For `σ -> 0`: Converges to degree centrality (only local information) For large `σ`: Identifies globally dominant nodes ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Competition parameter. If `None` (default), automatically computed from smallest eigenvalue and alpha. Higher values increase global competition for dominance. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Alpha parameter for auto-computing sigma (`sigma = alpha / |λ_min|`). Only used if sigma is `None`. Must be positive. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["iterative"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Solution method. Currently only "iterative" is implemented. (Analytical method may be added in the future for small graphs.) [tolerance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-05]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance for iterative solver. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum iterations for Newton's method. [patience]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of steps between convergence checks. Must satisfy `max_iter > 3 * patience`. [max_depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[50]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum bisection steps for finding smallest eigenvalue (when auto-computing sigma). [return_sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return (centrality_dict, sigma) tuple or (Graph, sigma) tuple instead of just dict or Graph. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`domirank_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float] or tuple[dict[int, float], float] or Graph or tuple[Graph, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True` and `return_sigma` is `False`: dictionary mapping node IDs to dominance scores. If `return_dict` is `True` and `return_sigma` is `True`: tuple of (centrality dict, sigma value). If `return_dict` is `False` and `return_sigma` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. If `return_dict=` is `False` and `return_sigma` is `True`: tuple of (self, sigma value). Nodes with positive scores are dominant; negative scores indicate submissive nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If alpha <= `0`, `dt` not in `(0, 1)`, tolerance <= `0`, or max_iter <= `3*patience`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} DomiRank (Engsig, Tejedor, Portillo, and Moreno, 2024) is a *competitive* centrality: rather than rewarding proximity to important neighbors as eigenvector-family metrics do, it rewards nodes that suppress their neighbors' scores. The continuous-time dynamics $\dot\Gamma_i = \sigma(d_i - \sum_j A_{ij}\Gamma_j) - \Gamma_i$ settle into a steady state where high-degree nodes surrounded by low-degree neighbors accumulate dominance, while nodes adjacent to already-dominant neighbors go into deficit (their scores drop below zero). Newton iteration solves the fixed-point equation in $O(E \cdot \text{iters})$ per step, which scales to networks of millions of edges. The `sigma=` parameter tunes the competition strength: as $\sigma \to 0$ the ranking degenerates to degree centrality, while large $\sigma$ surfaces the small set of globally dominant nodes. When `sigma=` is left unset, an internal bisection search picks $\sigma = \alpha / |\lambda_{\min}(A)|$, which is empirically near the sweet spot between local and global information. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Leaving `sigma=` unset auto-tunes the competition parameter from the graph's spectrum: ::: {#ccad083a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # Cycle ) graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {2: 0.4871792113533955, 3: 0.4871792113533955, 1: 0.4871792113533955} ``` ::: ::: Passing `return_sigma=True` alongside also returns the sigma value that was auto-selected: ::: {#3b2963e4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} domirank, sigma = graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True, return_sigma=True) sigma ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.95 ``` ::: ::: Manually raising `sigma=` increases competition and favors globally dominant nodes, while lowering it moves the result closer to plain degree centrality: ::: {#67167599 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") ) graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True, sigma=2.0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: 0.6666665181078656, 3: 0.6666665181078656, 1: 0.6666665181078656} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#d6c1717b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True, sigma=0.1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {2: 0.09090967551982432, 3: 0.09090967551982432, 1: 0.09090967551982432} ``` ::: :::
